title: Court records shed light on fatal police shooting of Brantford man
article: A Brantford man fatally shot by an OPP officer after a police pursuit east of Chatham last summer was a young father with a history of run-ins with police, according to court records and his obituary.

Ontario's police watchdog charged OPP Const. Sean O'Rourke, 54, last month with manslaughter and criminal negligence causing death in the deadly encounter along Highway 401 on July 7, 2020. The 24-year OPP veteran is to make his first appearance in a Chatham court Wednesday.
The Special Investigations Unit never released the name of the deceased, but recently filed court documents identify him as Nicholas Edward Grieves of Brantford.

Grieves, who died three days shy of his 25th birthday, leaves a two-year-old son, according to his obituary. "Nicholas will forever remain in our hearts, never to be forgotten and will always be loved by many," the obituary reads.
Several of Grieves' friends and relatives declined or didn't respond to interview requests.

Grieves had done several stints in jail over the years after convictions on charges including assault, obstructing police, possessing drugs for trafficking, robbery, possessing stolen property and unlawful entry.

Most recently, he was sentenced to 15 months in jail in 2019 after pleading guilty to robbery and assault after a violent robbery in Brantford two years before. A court heard how three men dragged a 31-year-old man into a home and threatened him with a gun, demanding he turn over his bank card and password.

During a 2017 encounter with Brantford police, officers used a stun gun to subdue Grieves after he resisted arrest and reached for a 10-centimetre hunting knife concealed in his pants. He later tried to bite an officer at hospital, where he also spat in the face of an emergency room nurse, a court heard.
Grieves was sentenced to a year in jail after pleading guilty to possessing drugs for trafficking, obstructing a police officer, assault and breaching court orders.
Grieves was fatally shot after Chatham-Kent OPP officers responded to a report of a gasoline theft and began following a vehicle west on the 401, the SIU said.
The car ended up in the ditch near the London Highgate exit, where an officer approached the vehicle and shot the driver, the SIU said.
O'Rourke, who has served in Chatham-Kent since 2004, has been suspended with pay since the SIU charged him Jan. 14.
The OPP Association, the union representing OPP officers and civilian staffers, has pledged to support O'Rourke.
"It was an absolutely tragic event," the association said in a news release. "Our lawyers will vigorously defend the actions of our officer in a court of law."
The SIU probes all cases of gunfire, death, serious injury and allegations of sexual assault involving police officers.
